questions.q: In this lab's design, why is extra_approval_threshold defined as a flow variable rather than a data pill?
options: Because it's a business rule value with no upstream record source, defined once by the designer instead of pulled from the trigger or a prior step
Because data pills cannot hold numeric values
Because flow variables are required inside every For Each loop
Because the trigger record already exposes a threshold field
questions.explain: The $1,000 threshold is a constant the organization sets, not something that exists on any record, so it belongs in the Flow Variables panel.

questions.q: What does the Look Up Records step in this design produce, and why does the flow need it?
options: A single-record pill with just the Request's own fields
A multi-record pill of every Requested Item tied to the approved Request, needed because the For Each must iterate over it
A flow variable representing the number of items on the Request
Nothing -- the For Each can iterate directly over the trigger record
questions.explain: The Requested Item detail doesn't live on the trigger record, so a Look Up Records step pulls it as a list pill for the For Each to loop over.

questions.q: A Request has three Requested Items: $400, $1,500, and $250. How many times does the If branch (extra approval) fire?
options: Three times, once per item
Zero times, because none of the items individually exceed the Request's total
Once, for the $1,500 item, since only it exceeds the $1,000 threshold
Twice, for the two cheaper items
questions.explain: The If/Else evaluates per current item inside the loop; only the $1,500 item's price exceeds the threshold, so only that pass takes the If branch.

questions.q: Why is the Create Record (fulfillment task) action placed inside the For Each loop body rather than after it?
options: So it runs exactly once total regardless of how many items exist
So it runs once per Requested Item, producing one fulfillment task per item on every pass
Because Create Record actions are not allowed outside a loop
Because the task needs the trigger's Number pill, not a current-item pill
questions.explain: Placing it inside the loop body ties task creation to each individual item, so N items produce N fulfillment tasks.

questions.q: For a Request with one $2,000 laptop and one $50 cable, how many fulfillment tasks exist once the flow finishes?
options: One, because only the laptop needed extra approval
Zero, because the cable never reaches the Create Record step
Two, because the For Each loop runs once per item and both items reach the Create Record step regardless of which branch they took
Four, because each item triggers both branches
questions.explain: Both items pass through the loop once each; the If/Else only decides whether extra approval happens first, and both branches still lead to a fulfillment task being created.
